newsitem.title: UK: Rates weak across freight market, BFI down again.
newsitem.headline: Rates weak across freight market, BFI down again.

text.p: The Baltic Freight Index fell four more points to 1,011 on Wednesday despite a good volume of fixtures.

Shipbrokers said rates remained weak in virtually all areas and there were again few hopeful signs for owners. They cited an unconfirmed report that Dreyfus may have fixed a Caper for early October for wheat St Lawrence/ARA at under $5.
No significant new US Gulf/Japan fixture was heard so far on Wednesday.

The only possible comfort generally for owners seemed to be that the volume of inquiry and fixture had begun to pick up lately as the drop in freight values of the last few weeks has continued. BIFFEX futures were again firmer on Wednesday reflecting what one broker called "a bit more confidence in the market" because of this volume of activity. Most-traded October was up 17 at 1,140 in volume of 104 lots by London's midday, extending a modest short covering rally. November put on 38 to 1,236 but in thin trade of just 30 lots.
